questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a quorum-based mutual exclusion algorithm?

answers.a: To ensure that only one process can access a critical section at a time.
answers.b: To allow multiple processes to access a critical section simultaneously.
answers.c: To reduce the number of messages exchanged.
answers.d: To eliminate the need for a central coordinator.

explanations.a: Correct. This is the fundamental goal of any mutual exclusion algorithm.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This is the opposite of mutual exclusion.
explanations.c: Incorrect. While some algorithms are more efficient, this is not the primary purpose.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is a characteristic of decentralized algorithms, but not the primary purpose.

questions.question: In Maekawa's algorithm, a process sends a request message to which set of processes?

answers.a: All processes in its own quorum.
answers.c: A randomly selected subset of processes.

explanations.a: Correct. A process only needs to communicate with the processes in its quorum.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This would defeat the purpose of using quorums for efficiency.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The quorum is a specific, not random, set of processes.

questions.question: A process can enter the critical section only after it receives a grant message from which set of processes?

answers.b: A majority of processes in the system.

explanations.a: Correct. A process must get permission from all members of its quorum.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The requirement is based on the quorum, not a simple majority of all processes.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Permission from one process is not sufficient.
explanations.d: Incorrect. There is no central coordinator.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of Maekawa's algorithm over Lamport's and Ricart-Agrawala's algorithms?

answers.a: It has a lower message complexity.

explanations.a: Correct. It reduces the message complexity from O(N) to O(sqrt(N)).
explanations.b: Incorrect. The concept of quorums can make it more complex to implement.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The basic algorithm is not fault-tolerant.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Timestamps are typically needed to handle deadlocks.

questions.question: The condition that any two quorums have a non-empty intersection ensures which property of mutual exclusion?

explanations.a: Correct. Safety (nothing bad happens) is ensured because any two processes wanting to enter the critical section will have to get permission from at least one common process.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Liveness (something good eventually happens) can be violated by deadlock.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Fairness is not guaranteed without additional mechanisms.

questions.question: If a process fails in Maekawa's algorithm, what is the potential consequence?

answers.b: The critical section may be accessed by multiple processes simultaneously.
answers.c: The failed process will be automatically removed from all quorums.
answers.d: The algorithm will continue to function correctly without any issues.

explanations.a: Correct. If a process fails, other processes may wait indefinitely for a message from it, leading to deadlock.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The safety property is generally not violated by a single failure.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The algorithm does not have an automatic mechanism for this.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Process failure can cause significant problems.

questions.question: How does Maekawa's algorithm handle concurrent requests for the critical section?

answers.a: It uses timestamps to order the requests.
answers.b: It grants access on a first-come, first-served basis.
answers.c: It can lead to deadlock if not handled carefully.
answers.d: It uses a central coordinator to resolve conflicts.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Timestamps are used to resolve deadlocks, not as the primary ordering mechanism in the basic algorithm.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The order of granting depends on the individual processes in the quorums, which can lead to deadlock.
explanations.c: Correct. Concurrent requests can create circular dependencies, leading to deadlock.
explanations.d: Incorrect. It is a decentralized algorithm.

questions.question: To build a fault-tolerant version of Maekawa's algorithm, what modification could be made?

answers.a: Increase the size of the quorums.
answers.c: Add a failure detector and a recovery mechanism.

explanations.a: Incorrect. While related to fault tolerance, this alone is not a complete solution.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This is one possible approach, but not the only one.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This is a key component, but other modifications may be needed.
explanations.d: Correct. A combination of techniques is often required to make the algorithm resilient to failures.

questions.question: Compared to a centralized mutual exclusion algorithm, Maekawa's algorithm offers better:

explanations.a: Correct. It avoids a single point of failure and reduces the bottleneck, improving scalability and reliability.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Centralized algorithms are generally simpler.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Centralized algorithms can be more efficient in low-contention scenarios.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The basic algorithm does not guarantee freedom from deadlock.
